h3. Forecasts Comparison (Marketplace Model vs GSheets)

Marketplace model forecasts generated with code from this [PR|https://github.com/bolteu/data-science-databricks/pull/607], matching logic from GSheets for calculation of incremental monthly active riders and churns (monthly uplift = weekly uplift * 4).

Results are matching between the marketplace model forecasts and GSheets for most metrics, with exception of *rider activations / churns* and *conversion models* (although the divergence is quite small). For riders models, the metrics diverge on the *base model*, which is probably caused by the recent changes in those models.

Still, the overall impact of these divergences is very small (≈0.02% for reactivations/churns, ~0% for active riders), which should not be a problem.

[Notebook for marketplace model and GSheets forecasts comparison|https://bolt-incentives.cloud.databricks.com/editor/notebooks/931797521221232?o=2472566184436351]

h3. Accuracy Comparison Between Both Aggregation Methods

A simple accuracy backtesting was run comparing both methods for monthly incremental rider activations / churns:

* Current method: weekly → monthly conversion using daily seasonality 
* GSheets method: monthly uplift = weekly uplift * 4

A backtest was run with the current codebase (label: {{test_new_rider_activations_churns_models}}), and another using the updated logic to match the one from GSheets (label: {{test_incremental_riders_aggregation_gsheet_logic}}).

We measure the average MAE on rider activations and churns by forecast horizon across all LTO cities, and the average MAPE for active riders.

Results are to follow once the backtest runs are finished and verified - will do it tomorrow first thing in the morning.

Hi [~accountid:712020:b3dbddb5-16a8-4ad6-9138-80fbe6e695a9], 

Here is the agreement we have in place with Hertz: [https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1GKtdKnozdNGgnv15L-D_cmwipHSim-an|https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1GKtdKnozdNGgnv15L-D_cmwipHSim-an|smart-link] 

 Bolt’s MRG obligations are included in the following sections: 

* Section 5.5: The MRG Period starts from the earlier of:
** actual completion of the branding work; or
** one working day after the vehicle was made available for branding.
* Section 5.6 & 5.7: During the MRG Period:
** Bolt guarantees minimum monthly revenue per Branded Vehicle.
** The guarantee ends when the vehicle is unbranded, removed from the program, or when the cap of €3,000 is reached.
* Section 8: MRG Shortfall is calculated monthly and billed by Hertz.
* Section 11.2: MRG shortfall liability is expressly excluded from the liability cap, highlighting that it's a standalone contractual commitment



I understand from the request that they would like to move the MRG from pre-branding to post-branding (car is branded only after the driver picks it up). This affects the point at which the MRG Period starts. If the branding never occurs, the car never becomes a Branded Vehicle, and the MRG does not apply.



Essentially, the +*question is*+: *Can Bolt stop making MRG Payments?*

→ I think that yes, Bolt can stop MRG payments prospectively for vehicles that are not branded. Per the contract:

* Only Branded Vehicles trigger the MRG obligation.
* Vehicles that are never branded (i.e., if the branding is skipped or cancelled) never enter an MRG Period.
* Therefore, no MRG payment obligation arises.

However, if a vehicle has already been branded (before or after rental), and notice per section 5.5 was given, then the MRG obligation applies retroactively from that point until unbranding or reaching the cap.



+*Recommendation*+

→ First step would be to check with the business whether this has been discussed and agreed with the partner (I will check this).

h4. 1. *If Hertz Has Been Informed and Agreed*:

* Proceed with a formal amendment to the Country Addendum (France).
* This should:
** Confirm that branding occurs only post-rental.
** State that no car is deemed branded unless branding is physically completed and notified under Clause 5.5.
** Acknowledge that vehicles not branded will not trigger MRG.

h4. 2. *If Hertz Has Not Yet Been Informed or Has Not Agreed*:

There are some contractual risks:

* We cannot proceed with a unilateral change as this would breach the agreement, especially if:
** Hertz incurred costs assuming pre-branded availability.
** Vehicles were deemed branded based on prior Bolt forecasts (Clause 5.1) and MRG was expected.
* If this is actioned without an amendment signed by both parties, we could face:
** Potential claim for breach of contract.
** Loss of use or other indirect loss claims from Hertz if branded vehicles remain unrented.
** Reputational risk and strain on partnership.


What are your thoughts on this?

Thank you in advance for your review ! 🙏

Hey Team,

We asked our external counsels avise about this and, essentially, the information provided is that *notifying fleets* when couriers are suspended is generally acceptable, but the framing should avoid looking like a disciplinary process. The appeal option increases risk but may be justified under DSA/P2B. Keep language factual and directed at fleets as the contracting party.



For your visibility, this is the exact question we asked and the exact reply we received:

*Question:* _Another topic we would like you to review is regarding communications to Fleets when their couriers get terminated or suspended._
_Specifically, we would like to know if the following email and reasons for termination or suspension are OK to be subject to a communication:_

_The email would have the following structure:_

*_Subject line:_* _Termination of courier access_
*_Headline:_* _Courier’s access to Bolt Food was terminated_
*_Intro:_* _Hello *|Profile - first_name|*!_
*_Courier info and block duration:_* _The access of [Courier Full Name] to the Bolt Food Platform has been terminated. We are notifying you as this courier’s access is associated with your fleet account._

*_Block reasons possible to apply and respective text:_*
*_Courier Changed Order Status Incorrectly_* _- The courier has repeatedly updated the order status incorrectly during deliveries. This interferes with the arrangement of services via the Bolt Food Platform, which is prohibited under our platform terms._

*_Courier contacting CS unnecessarily -_* _The courier has repeatedly contacted our support without a valid reason. This interferes with the arrangement of services via the Bolt Food Platform, which is prohibited under our platform terms._

*_Courier was late -_* _We've received some complaints that the courier’s deliveries are taking longer than estimated. Such delays can cause food safety risks for customers of the Bolt Food Platform, which is prohibited under our platform terms._

*_Didn't Pick Up Order -_* _We’ve received complaints that the courier is not picking up orders they’ve accepted. This interferes with the arrangement of services via the Bolt Food Platform and can cause food safety risks for customers, which is prohibited under our platform terms._

*_Eater Never Received the Order -_* _We've received reports of undelivered orders after pickup. This breaches our platform terms, which prohibit offering delivery services if you have no genuine intention to actually provide these services._

*_Suspected Fraud -_* _We detected suspicious activity that is indicative of fraudulent behaviour, which is prohibited under our platform terms._

*_Damaged Order -_* _We noticed some of the courier’s recent deliveries arrived damaged and unfit for consumption. Damaging the order can cause food safety risks for customers of the Bolt Food Platform, which is prohibited under our platform terms._

*_Courier Ignored Eater's Note -_* _We recently received reports from users saying their delivery instructions weren't followed. Such behaviour causes safety risks for other users of the Bolt Food Platform, which is prohibited under our platform terms._

*_Re-dispatch request during an active order -_* _The courier has frequently requested a re-dispatch during an active order on several occasions. Re-dispatches are available for situations that genuinely prevent order completion. Frequent and recurring re-dispatches without a genuine reason can cause order delays and negatively impact our customer experience due to misleading delivery time estimates. Also, our platform terms forbid offering services without a genuine intention to actually fulfil those services._

*_Fallback option -_* _We’ve received some complaints that the courier is not following our platform terms._

*_Appeals:_* _By this notice, we are terminating the courier’s access to the Bolt Food platform associated with your fleet account with immediate effect. From this point forward, you no longer have the right to allow the courier to access or use the Bolt platform._

_We have reviewed the courier’s recent activity, including previous instances of breaching our platform terms, and consider this termination to be appropriate and permitted under the termination provisions of our platform terms._

_However, you can appeal this decision within the next 6 months. To do so, please contact our Support Team or submit a form via the Notices and Complaints section of our website._

_Learn More_

_We appreciate your understanding and cooperation in this matter._

_Best regards,_
_The Bolt Food team_

*DLA Piper:* _As previously advised, in itself, the process of_ *_notifying the fleet of the blocking, stating the reasons for the same, and referring to an appeal process already poses risks_*_, to the extent that it establishes what could be considered a disciplinary procedure, which is particularly emphasised by the existence of an appeal body - in other words, this is not strictly speaking a purely ‘contractual’ decision, but more a decision of a sanctioning nature, so much so that it can be reconsidered by the company following an appeal. We have previously advised that the appeal body should be removed, but we understand that the existence of the appeal body may be a requirement imposed by DSA, which can also be used as an argument in Bolt’s favour._

_In any case, these risks are mitigated when the communication is made to the fleet. From our experience in reclassification trials, with the notification being sent to fleets, couriers are not aware of this notification and the reasons for blocking, and such a notification has never been mentioned._

Hi all 👋

On the liability cap, I think this is one of those “_technically not great, but practically low risk_” situations.

The cap is set at the contract value (~£25k), which on paper looks small if you imagine a worst-case scenario. However, this is a UK event, so the _NHS_ _should_ cover the medical treatment, so we shouldn’t be exposed to huge hospital bills. Any real exposure would be compensation-style claims (pain, suffering, loss of earnings, etc.).

Since it’s our own employees attending, our Employer’s Liability cover would likely respond if Bolt were held responsible. If Evolve were at fault, their insurance should apply, although it would be capped by these terms.

Normally, I would suggest pushing back on such a low cap, but looking at the event, there does not appear to be any high-risk activities; i.e. _no cliff-jumping, fire-eating, or tiger wrestling,_ etc. So I would consider this a very low risk event. 

However, I am just an insurance nerd and not responsible for risk to the business. So if the business is not comfortable accepting this, I think we have three options:



# Accept the cap as is and rely on the NHS, plus our existing insurances, and accept this small risk.
# Negotiate with Evolve and push for the cap to match their £10m public liability cover.
# We buy a bolt-on cover (no pun intended) for a short-term event liability policy that protects Bolt directly.

But, from an insurance perspective, I do not think it is a deal-breaker, and it comes down to how cautious we want to be as a business.

Response to Complaint - Case ID WO250823438788

{quote}Dear Sir/Madam,

We acknowledge receipt of the complaint submitted by Mr. Waralak Sarajit concerning a disputed payment on the Bolt platform.

Our review indicates that during the trip (approx. 08:00–08:45 AM), the rider selected card payment for the fare of 556 THB. The driver, not noticing this, also collected the same amount in cash, in addition to a 75 THB toll fee. This led to duplicate payment of the fare (cash + card) for the same trip in the amount of 556 THB. 

In line with policy, only the 20 THB commission fee was available for adjustment. The driver declined this resolution, stating it was not fair. The driver stated that only a toll fee of 75 THB was collected in cash and disputed responsibility for the duplicate charge.

Bolt’s systems confirmed the card payment of 556 THB. Because cash payments are offline, the platform cannot independently verify the alleged duplicate cash transaction or the toll payment. 

In line with procedure, the agent refunded the rider 556 THB by deducting this amount from the driver’s account. While the driver disputed this outcome, our system can only track the 556 THB card transaction; both the cash fare and the toll payment are offline transactions and therefore not independently verifiable.

Respectfully,
Bolt Support Services (Thailand) Co., Ltd.{quote}

To summarize: 

# Any “bonus” payments for fleet couriers should go directly to fleets, and not to fleet couriers. Fleets have to distribute the bonuses themselves.
# If we send out comms to fleet couriers in relation to campaigns, then it has to be clear that the campaign is ran by the fleet (even though Bolt is ultimately the one who funds the campaign - this will not be mentioned in the comms). I would like to review the comms once they are ready. 
# The comms have to make it clear that it’s a voluntary bonus and there cannot be any “obligatory” elements (e.g. NO “you have to have” an AR of 80, but rather “if you have 80% AR”) 
# This will add an additional layer of reclassification risk - although we are framing the bonus as a “fleet incentive”, then ultimately this can be interpreted as Bolt exercising control over fleet couriers, especially since we are actually funding the campaign. 
# When performance targets (KPIs) are set and measured only at the *fleet level*, Bolt can credibly argue that it has *no direct relationship with or control over individual couriers*. The fleet owner is the one responsible for managing their couriers, including how they meet those KPIs. This separation is useful in defending against reclassification claims, because if Bolt only sets standards for fleets (our contractual counterparties), we can say we are simply a platform contracting with another business, not directly managing couriers.
However, once we start running *targeted campaigns aimed directly at couriers* — for example, “accept 80% of orders this week and get a €100 bonus” — the picture changes. Even if the fleet sends the comms, then Bolt is ultimately the one payng for rewards tied to *personal KPIs* like acceptance rate or hours online. Therefore, when implementing this is markets where KPIs are set at a fleet level (e.g. RO), then this increases reclassification risk additionally.

''Your business company operates under the *Resale Billing Model*. This means that each ride is first invoiced from the fleet to the Bolt entity (that is why you can see the fleet’s name on the ride invoice). Bolt then resells these rides to the business company through a single aggregated monthly invoice.

According to tax requirements, when Bolt resells the ride to the business company, VAT must be applied even if the fleet is not VAT-liable. For example:

* Net ride fare: €9.75
* VAT (25%): €2.00
* Total on invoice: €11.75

This is why the amount charged on the aggregated invoice may differ from the net ride fare visible on the company dashboard. The VAT charges are reflected and clearly itemised in your *monthly aggregated invoice*.

Please note that this VAT is not an additional fee retained by Bolt but a *statutory tax obligation*. If your company is VAT-registered, you may be able to reclaim this VAT as input tax in your accounting records.''

Updating mapping rules for existing transactions will lead to conflicts:

# Previously transaction had been saved with old mapping rules.
# Same transaction is received after mapping rules have been updated: it have different values in its fields (because mapping rules changed), but the same key.

This will cause the conflict: two transactions with the same key, but different field values.



There could be 4 ways to solve it:

# Just leave mappings as they are. Don’t change them. BoG doesn’t use separators at all. LHV continues to use old separator {{/}}, Citi will use new separator {{:||:}}.
# Change mappings and then resolve conflicts manually, hoping that there will be not many of them. Currently conflicts will happen for LHV only. If we will not do backfills, then conflicts will only happen for one day when new mappings are deployed. We can avoid them if we would turn off receiving LHV intraday statements for that one day, and then turn it on again.
# Keep both mapping rules: old and new, but separate them by date: old mappings are used for transactions with book date before some date X, and new mappings are used for transactions with book date after same date X. Then there will be no conflicts, but both mapping rules (old and new one) will be in the code and in the data forever.
# Delete all the transactions and then reprocess all the statements from S3 (we don’t need to request them from bank).

Taking all this into account I would recommend just don’t change the mappings for those connectors for which there are already transactions in our DB unless there is a really good reason for it.

If we really need to change the mappings and there are already many transactions in our DB with old mappings, then I believe that option 3 is the best way to go (no conflicts, no need to delete everything and reprocess). And I think that it is the only feasible way when we have our transactions exported to other systems, because we are not able to change the history in all the systems. Thus we need to keep old transactions with old mappings, and parse new transactions with new mappings.

And the question is: do we *really* need to change separator for LHV from {{/}} to {{:||:}}?

Hi all, after some investigation, we found that the issues where the user receives push notifications in the wrong language are not always related. They can be caused by different problems:

# User changing the language on one Eater app, which also updates the server language, but on the Eater app in their other devices, it’s unchanged.
# The server code gets the language from Rider app but sends the notification to Eater app.
# The content for the push notification was defined in the wrong language.

We’ll be using this item to fix #1, by synchronizing the language set by the user across all their apps. When this item is finished, it does not mean that all the issues linked to this issue are fixed, as they may be caused by other things. Going forward, we should investigate each specific issue separately.

hi [~accountid:712020:ca818823-efac-45fe-ba7d-a6686a5e08b5] [~accountid:712020:e6db7bf1-81f8-43b5-b50b-2b4bb57ce924]

*Previous idea:* 

It was confirmed by external legal that using Queen Silvia's personality for advertisement would be an unnecessary high risk and they advise against it.

*Gustav Vasa idea:* 

The main areas of potential risk: 

*(i)  defamation of the deceased - Low risk* 

* Legal framework: Under the Swedish Penal Code (Sw. _Brottsbalken_), it can constitute defamation to disparage a deceased person in a way that is offensive to surviving relatives.
* Since Gustav Vasa has been deceased for centuries, it is rather unlikely that any surviving relatives could be considered affected within the meaning of the statute of the Penal Code. In addition, Swedish courts generally recognize that public figures - including politicians, celebrities and monarchs - are subject to critical and humorous reinterpretations and are therefore afforded a lower level of protection in practice. 

*(ii) compliance with good marketing practices - Low risk* 

Using a national historical figure in a comedic context could be seen as inappropriate by some and might lead to complaints to the Swedish Advertising Ombudsman or Consumer Agency. While fines are unlikely, decisions are public and could impact reputation. Gustav Vasa’s name is also linked to well-known brands and institutions (e.g. Vasa Museum), implying their endorsement without involvement could be considered misleading under the Swedish Marketing Act. However, based on the current campaign outline, this risk is low.

*(iii) copyright and cultural protection  - Low or Medium Risk*   

* Your concept involves an actor impersonating Gustav Vasa.
* Any original 16th-century artworks, portraits, or depictions of Gustav Vasa are no longer protected by copyright. However, according to the Swedish Copyright Act (Sw. _Upphovsrättslagen)_, Swedish authorities may prohibit the use of a literary or artistic work *if it is reproduced in a way that violates cultural interests*. Although this rule is rarely applied, it exists to protect works of high cultural significance and could, in theory, apply to important historical depictions of Gustav Vasa. 

*Cultural and Historical aspect from the script, discussed with Swedish Legal* [~accountid:712020:7f47c2af-14e1-4206-a795-ac87cb906276]

While Sweden and Denmark have a long history of rivalry, referencing past violent conflicts—like the Stockholm Bloodbath—in a commercial context risks trivializing sensitive history and may be seen as offensive. This could create unnecessary controversy and distract from our Safety campaign. It is also concerning as we’ve just launched in Denmark and want to build positive brand associations. A lighter approach, focusing on friendly stereotypes or cultural quirks, would be more appropriate.

*Next steps:* 

* The script in its current form raises concerns from both a PR, Policy, and overall brand-perception perspective. While not a strictly legal matter, it risks unnecessary controversy and may distract from our intended message, especially given our recent launch in Denmark where we want to build positive associations.
* To address this, [~accountid:712020:7f47c2af-14e1-4206-a795-ac87cb906276]  will create a group chat with PR, Policy, and the Rides GM so this can be discussed with all relevant stakeholders and the potential impact carefully considered.

Hi team, 

The user is reporting a double-charge because of incremental authorization.
Incremental authorization in card payments refers to the process of requesting an additional authorization on a customer’s card when the original authorized amount is insufficient to cover the final transaction cost. This typically happens in scenarios where the final amount of the transaction is not known upfront or may change.

I have checked the case and everything looks good on Bolt’s end. The pre-authorization has been released to the customer. 
You can ask the customer to reach out to their bank in order to confirm the authorized funds have been released. Their bank can locate the funds with the authorization date and amount. 


Please let me know if you have any other questions.

Cheers,

# Background

Denisa from the recruitment team reached out with a request related to job postings on a Bulgarian job board. The board requires a data privacy contact to be added and confirmed before ads can be published. Without this, postings cannot go live, and the requirement was only communicated after the team had already paid for advertising. h3. Accuracy Comparison Between Both Aggregation Methods

The performance evaluation from the backtests using the two suggested aggregation methods (current one - week to month aggregation using daily seasonality - and matching GSheets logic - monthly uplift = weekly uplift * 4) shows that performance is actually better overall when using the simpler GSheets logic. Results were evaluated on 1, 3 and 12 month horizons and on the following metrics:

* Rider Activations %
* Rider Churns %
* Active Riders
* Finished Orders

h3. Results

Results are separated by target metric, horizon and show the change in performance (MAE for rider activations and churns, MAPE for active riders and finished orders, all aggregated as averages for all LTO cities weighted by their respective GMV) between the current method to the proposed one, as well as the share of cities that had an improvement in accuracy:

h4. Rider Activations %

* *1M:* 1.78% → 1.28% (76% of cities improved)
* *3M:* 1.87% → 1.23% (73% of cities improved)
* *12M:* 1.92% → 1.23% (65% of cities improved)

h4. Rider Churns %

* *1M:* 1.11% → 1.23% (59% of cities improved)
* *3M:* 1.19% → 1.36% (60% of cities improved)
* *12M:* 1.18% → 1.52% (70% of cities improved)

h4. Active Riders

* *1M:* 3.96% → 3.26% (64% of cities improved)
* *3M:* 5.52% → 4.44% (61% of cities improved)
* *12M:* 10.82% → 9.11% (61% of cities improved)

h4. Finished Orders

* *1M:* 9.84% → 10.02% (59% of cities improved)
* *3M:* 10.21% → 9.63% (63% of cities improved)
* *12M:* 13.95% → 10.26% (61% of cities improved)

h3. Conclusion

The method for aggregating incremental rider activations and churns that gives the best overall accuracy is the simpler method (weekly uplift * 4); by changing the method in the codebase we also make it compatible to what we have in GSheets, and it’s highly recommended that we make this change. Based on what’s been shared and on information I gathered from previous responses sent to the AMT on the taxi topic, I believe we can say that:

* The Bolt app does not calculate taxi prices simultaneously on the basis of both time and distance. For metered-fare trips, the app shows only an indicative estimate based on the parameters set out in the legal regime, and the final price is always the amount shown on the taximeter, in accordance with Decree-Law no. 101/2023 and the applicable Fare Convention.
* The estimates shown in the app take into account the route predicted by the navigation system and may vary depending on direction of travel, traffic or other momentary conditions. That is why displayed amounts can differ. The screenshots show different estimates because the routes being compared are also different, which naturally creates variation (e.g., traffic lights, one-way streets, traffic).
* Bolt fully complies with Decree-Law no. 101/2023 and the Fare Convention in force and, under either regime, the app ensures transparency by providing users with clear information on the selected category and the price estimate before the trip is confirmed:
- Metered fare: when the user requests a ride, the Bolt platform provides the user and the taxi driver with a price range estimate for the trip, taking into account the applicable legislation. This range is provided for indicative purposes only and is not binding on either the taxi operator or the user.
Once the service is completed, the final price must be the amount shown on the taximeter, which the driver (on behalf of the taxi operator) enters on the Bolt platform and communicates to the passenger.
- Contract fare (Tariff C): also provided for in Article 18 of Decree-Law no. 101/2023 and in the Fare Convention, the price is pre-defined between the taxi operator and the user.

Hi [~accountid:712020:238a1b89-0f1b-4797-9066-90af4142a510] I can jump in on this for the privacy side.

* If push comes to shove, we can definitely argue that Bolt is *_not_* in breach of the UK GDPR and P2B regulation here. In particular:
** UK GDPR - We have already provided the driver with access to their personal data, as requested. The passenger fare is as much the _passenger’s_ personal data as it is the driver’s, and so it is not as simple as saying we should provide this in all cases.
** P2B Reg - This requires Bolt to _explain_ in the T&Cs _whether_ the driver can access certain personal data - it does _not_ amount to a right to access that data.
* Indeed, I understand that there is a reason why we do not typically share passenger fares with drivers (I cannot recall off the top of my head - happy to look into this further but I suggest you sync with the Regional Legal team first in case it is obvious to them). If we need to respond in detail on this, we can consider that point.
* In any case, *I would not recommend responding to this allegation in detail for now* (/)  Particularly because:
** The driver is clearly not interested in their privacy rights here - they have in the past made various allegations (including regarding automated decision-making) which the driver has dropped in recent correspondence. As such, it is reasonable to assume they are throwing a lot at the wall to see what sticks. 
** Given the tone of correspondence so far, the driver is not going to be satisfied with what we provide them in many cases. This is not a hill that we need to die on for now, and providing a detailed response on this issue is likely to just prompt further accusations / questions.

Hope this helps! If the complainant makes any further privacy law allegations then feel free to loop me in 🙂

Hello, [~accountid:712020:0c8dd65b-46d5-4dc0-b5bd-76209c1e8048]! I reviewed the most relevant Czech laws with ChatGPT support which I confirmed with available English versions as possible. +*My conclusion is that Bolt has no legal grounds to report such an incident to the relevant authorities.*+ 

However, we should also pay attention to the DSA regulation (Regulation (EU) 2022/2065) which generally may oblige Bolt to implement some restrictions on the User in connection with unlawful content provided by them in the Bolt app. *To confirm whether and how we should proceed with DSA restrictions towards the User I would need more time to review and probably to contact the external counsel (please confirm* [~accountid:5e0f07ab9a4b780d990e9fb9] *if there would be such a necessity with regards to my current workload - I could handle it next week, at the earliest).* :loading: 

Please bear in mind that for the need of checking this matter I haven’t involved yet any Czech ext. counsel to confirm 100% my conclusions. [~accountid:712020:0c8dd65b-46d5-4dc0-b5bd-76209c1e8048] If you still feel the external is necessary for reporting purposes, please let me know. 🙂 

Here’s the backbone of my conclusions:

# *Czech Criminal Code (Act No. 40/2009 Coll.)*
#* Yes, propagating or expressing sympathy for extremist movements *can be a crime* (§ 403–§ 405).
#* But the separate offence of failure to report a crim_e_ (§ 368) lists the specific crimes you must report. The crimes specified in § 403, § 404, § 405 are not included in that reporting duty. Conclusion: even if the user’s selfie could amount to § 403–§ 405, there’s no §368 obligation on Bolt to notify the police.
# *DSA (Regulation (EU) 2022/2065), Article 18*
#* Hosting providers must inform law-enforcement *only when* they become aware of information giving rise to a suspicion of a criminal offence involving a *threat to the life or safety of a person.* Mere display of extremist symbols typically *won’t* meet that “life or safety” threshold, so Art. 18 *doesn’t force a report* in your fact pattern.
# *Terrorist content rules (especially Art. 3 of the Regulation (EU) 2021/784)*
#* There is a *one-hour removal* obligation *upon a formal removal order* for terrorist content - this is about taking down, not a general proactive reporting duty. Again, *extremist symbols that aren’t terrorist content and aren’t subject to an order don’t trigger a report*. 
# *Czech E-commerce framework (Act No. 480/2004 Coll.)*
#* Sets safe-harbor/no-general-monitoring rules for hosting/online services; *no blanket duty to report* user content to authorities.

 Best,

I ran some accuracy checks across cities and horizons, and here’s the summary:

* For each city + horizon, I averaged metric performance.
* Then, for each horizon + metric, I took the median accuracy.
* Accuracy is either MAPE or MAE depending on the metric.

I focused on 3M horizon forecasts as for 12M the performance of some metrics gets really hurt (but that happens for both models).*Results are gathered in the table below:*

* Baseline = accuracy with the full training period (since Jan 2023).
* Backtest = accuracy when training on a reduced (~8 months) period.
* Abs diff = backtest – baseline (negative = accuracy improved, positive = accuracy worsened).

*Key takeaways:*

* Overall, performance is not heavily degraded. For example, _finished_orders_ accuracy is nearly unchanged.
* Some metrics get slightly worse, others even improve, but difference is usually not that big.
* Conversion metrics (o2f, s2o) remain stable as expected, since they’re not time-series models and thus less impacted by reduced training periods as they do not model trend/seasonality.
* All in all, training on ~8 months of data seems reasonable: we lose a bit of accuracy on some metrics, but not in a way that looks critical compared to using a bit more data for training.

[Databricks notebook|https://bolt-incentives.cloud.databricks.com/editor/notebooks/1523234471954876?o=2472566184436351].

*Conclusion:* It seems fair to use the IBM framework in newer markets (less than a year of data), we'll just lose some functionalities like backtesting and possibly the quality of incremental data will be low, but overall forecasting accuracy does not seem to deteriorate too much.

* allow auto scale

Given the fact that the facts occurred in 27.07.2022 and they are only notifying us now, we can invoke limitation.

Article 25/1 of the TVDE Law states that: _“Violations of the provisions of this law constitute administrative offences, and in all matters not specifically regulated herein, the general regime for administrative offences shall apply.”_

In it’s turn, the general regime for administrative offences states in its article 27.º that:

_”The administrative offence procedure shall be extinguished by limitation as soon as the following periods have elapsed since the administrative offence was committed:_
_a) Five years, in the case of an administrative offence to which a fine of (euro) 49,879.79 or more is applicable;_
_b) Three years, in the case of an administrative offence punishable by a fine of (euro) 2493.99 or more and less than (euro) 49879.79;_
_c) One year, in all other cases.”_

In this case, line b) is the one applicable and, since the facts occurred in July 2022, at this date three years already passed.

h4. Driver refused to carry an assistance animal or pet

{color:#bf2600}If not communicated, confirm if it was a pet or an assistance animal.{color}

----

*Assistance animal*

* Escalate case to Safety

*Pet*

* Check the Bolt [website|https://bolt.eu/en-lt/cities/] to confirm if the Pet category is available in their city
* Verify the category selected by the rider
** Pets category was *not selected*
*** Explain to the rider that their chosen category did not match their needs
*** If the category is *available* in their city, advise the rider on how to pick the correct category
*** If the category is *not available* in their city, advise the rider (if applicable) to call the driver next time and ask if they can take the pet

Refusing an assistance animal is illegal (unless the driver is exempt from carrying assistance animals due to health issues), while refusing an emotional support/regular animal is up to the driver. {color:#ff5630}*Neither Bolt nor the drivers should ask passengers to prove that their animal is an assistance animal.*{color}

Hi [~accountid:712020:1d4eb168-65d8-4fe2-9240-3537fd827409] if  sharing the requested data is not required under the dispatch operator licence then NTA has no statutory basis to force the disclosure

Bolt should cooperate, but *only after securing written assurances* that the information will be kept confidential. Once written confirmation is received, Bolt can  share the date but we suggest only sharing aggregated H1 2025 data.

Please find below draft email that can be sent to NTA (feel free to amend it): 

_Thank you for your email  and for the opportunity to contribute to the NTA’s survey on dispatch operations in Ireland. Bolt welcomes the constructive engagement with the NTA and supports efforts to build a more complete picture of the market._

_We note that a number of the datapoints requested are highly commercially sensitive. Before sharing this information, we would be grateful if the NTA could kindly confirm in writing that:_

* _Before providing the data, we would be grateful if you could kindly confirm in writing that:_
** _The data will be treated as confidential and commercially sensitive under all relevant Irish laws;_
** _The data will be used solely for policy and strategy development purposes, and not for enforcement or benchmarking;_
** _The data will not be disclosed to any third parties (including consultants) without Bolt’s prior written consent;_
** _Appropriate security measures will apply, and the data will be retained only as long as necessary for the stated purpose; and_
** _This disclosure is made on a voluntary basis and does not create any ongoing obligation for Bolt to provide further datasets._

_Once we have received confirmation of the above, we will be pleased to provide the requested survey data for H1 2025 in aggregate form only (e.g. averages, totals and percentages)._

_We trust this approach will strike the right balance between supporting the NTA’s important work and safeguarding Bolt’s legitimate commercial interests._

_We look forward to your confirmation.”_

TfL expects PHV operators to follow fair procedures when suspending or removing drivers — especially if this could affect their private hire licence or ability to work. Hi [~accountid:5acb1f48d8b95a2b34f150a8], just following up on this. I note that you discussed this with [~accountid:712020:209f6e12-e421-4fbf-9a9f-60d100117bab] and it was agreed that a *sole trader* can have a business bank account on the basis that we only allow drivers to submit a *sole trader business bank account* during via the driver registration. I too agree with this approach and have set out below my response to your follow-up question. 

+Is the most compliant path to allow drivers who want to submit a limited company bank account through our+ +*fleet registration flow?*+

With regards to handling drivers who want to submit a limited company bank account, I agree with [~accountid:712020:726e5ea0-027c-4c31-a0fd-2c23b80dc56c] that registering these drivers through our fleet registration flow seems to be the most logical/compliant solution (see further thoughts below if useful). 

+Thoughts on the different+ +*assumptions*+ +on the scenarios/combinations regarding accepting types of bank accounts+

I’ve reviewed the assumptions in the screenshot you kindly attached to this ticket and have set out my comments below. *In summary, from a Legal perspective, we’re aligned with the assumptions (and, subject to your analysis would probably change the “to decide” points to “Not Allowed”).* I’ve set out some further comments below if helpful. 

# *Community & Regular IC Drivers (individual driver flow):*
#* Sole trader business accounts are acceptable, as the contracting party and the account holder remain the same individual.
#* Limited company accounts are not acceptable, since they belong to a separate legal entity and would conflict with our contract being with the individual driver.
# *Fleets (business flow):*
#* Limited company accounts are appropriate, as the contracting party is the company itself and payments to its business account are legally consistent.
#* Sole trader accounts: while it is legally possible for a sole trader to operate as a fleet, in practice this creates operational confusion and undermines the clear distinction between “individual driver” and “fleet” registration models. For that reason, our recommendation is *not to accept sole trader accounts in the fleet flow* and to reserve the fleet channel for incorporated businesses.
# *Principal vs. Agency:*
#* The same logic applies in both models; what matters is the contracting entity (individual vs. company).

*In summary:*

* *Allowed:* (a) Sole trader accounts under individual driver flows and (b) Ltd company accounts under fleet flows.
* *Not Allowed:* (a) Ltd company accounts under driver flows and (b) sole trader accounts under fleet flows.

Let me know if you would like to discuss further. 

Best wishes

Adding my calculations here as an internal note just as reference: 

# If Bolt terminates in August 2026, the shortfall would be *EUR 1,500,000*.

Calculation: Since August 2026 falls "between September 2025 and August 2027, the Customer will pay ProcessOut an amount equivalent to the sum of the Flat Fee for the 12 calendar months in the term following the date of the Customer's termination notice"

* The 12 months following August 2026 would be September 2026 through August 2027.
* From "January 2026 until August 2028" the flat fee is "EUR 125,000" per month.

*Calculation:*

* 12 months × EUR 125,000 = *EUR 1,500,000*

This is a substantial penalty that essentially requires Bolt to pay for a full year of services they won't be using. This clearly conflicts with their intention to only pay for services actually used, making the suggested revisions to the termination provisions even more critical.

# If Bolt notifies termination in August 2028, the shortfall would be *EUR 0*.

Calculation:

# *Contract Term Ends*: The flat fee period runs "From 1 September 2025 until 31 August 2028", so the contract term naturally expires on August 31, 2028.
# *No Remaining Months*: Since August 2028 falls "between September 2027 and August 2028," the shortfall would be "the sum of the Flat Fee for the remaining calendar months in the term." But there are no remaining months after August 2028 within the contract term.
# *Natural Expiration*: The contract would expire on its own terms on August 31, 2028, regardless of any termination notice.

{color:#bf2600}However, there's a {color}{color:#bf2600}*potential complication*{color}{color:#bf2600}: The original Terms and Conditions require "6 month written notice" for termination. If Bolt gives notice in August 2028, the 6-month notice period would extend to February 2029, but the flat fee commitment only runs until August 2028.{color}

{color:#bf2600}This should be clarified in the amendment: what happens when the notice period extends beyond the flat fee commitment period? It would be good to add language clarifying that no shortfall applies if termination notice is given in the final months of the term.{color}

# If Bolt notifies termination in January 2027, the shortfall would be *EUR 1,500,000*.

Calculation:

Since January 2027 falls "between September 2025 and August 2027," the Customer must pay "an amount equivalent to the sum of the Flat Fee for the 12 calendar months in the term following the date of the Customer's termination notice."

The 12 months following January 2027 would be February 2027 through January 2028.

According to the pricing table, from "January 2026 until August 2028" the flat fee is "EUR 125,000" per month.

*Calculation:*

* 12 months × EUR 125,000 = *EUR 1,500,000*

This demonstrates how punitive the termination provisions are - whether Bolt terminates in August 2026 or January 2027 (5 months later), they still pay the same EUR 1,500,000 shortfall. The penalty structure essentially locks Bolt into paying for services through January 2028 regardless of when they terminate during this period, which directly conflicts with their goal of paying only for services actually used.

With the current wording, it seems Bolt will pay ProcessOut an amount equivalent to the sum of the Flat Fee for the 12 calendar months in the term following the date of the Customer’s termination notice. Termination notice is 6 months. Would it mean that Bolt will pay the flat fee for those 6 months until the termination, and the shortfall is for 12 additional months? The clause is poorly drafted and creates significant ambiguity.

*For January 2027 termination notice:*

# *Notice given*: January 2027
# *6-month notice period*: February 2027 - July 2027 (Bolt continues paying regular flat fees and using services)
# *Effective termination date*: August 1, 2027
# *Shortfall period*: The "12 calendar months following the notice date" would be February 2027 - January 2028
# *But*: Bolt already pays regular fees for February-July 2027 (6 months)
# *Therefore*: Shortfall should only be for August 2027 - January 2028 = *6 months × EUR 125,000 = EUR 750,000*

*The Problem*: The amendment language is ambiguous. It says "12 calendar months in the term following the date of the Customer's termination notice" rather than "following the effective date of termination."

*Recommendation*: This ambiguity needs to be clarified in the amendment because:

* ProcessOut might argue Bolt pays both regular fees during notice period AND the full 12-month shortfall
* This would result in double payment for overlapping periods

*We will first suggest to*: Clarify that the shortfall only covers months after the effective termination date, not during the notice period when services are still being provided and paid for. Secondly, we should address the question: {color:#bf2600}what happens when the notice period extends beyond the flat fee commitment period? {color}

# When the user first makes a payment, the bank temporarily ‘reserves’ the funds and this is just the bank setting aside the amount for the transaction. The user’s account balance might show less amount but the payment hasn’t actually been taken out by the bank yet.
# Later, when the payment is fully processed, that reserved amount is now “officially” debited from the user’s account. At that point, some banks send a second notification, which can make it seem like a second charge. They can either return the first charged amount and debit a new one or just keep the first reserved amount as final charge.

I would advise the user to check their final account balance or statement, where they can confirm that only one payment was actually withdrawn. The earlier “pending” amount will either drop off or convert into the final charge.

Hello Team!

I completely understand why this might look like a double charge, but I can assure you that the user was only charged once. This is a common part of how card payments are processed. Here's what happens:

# When the user first makes a payment, the bank temporarily ‘reserves' the funds and this is just the bank setting aside the amount for the transaction. The user’s account balance might show less amount but the payment hasn’t actually been taken out by the bank yet.
# Later, when the payment is fully processed, that reserved amount is now “officially” debited from the user’s account. At that point, some banks send a second notification, which can make it seem like a second charge.


I would advise the user to check their final account balance or statement, where they can confirm that only one payment was actually withdrawn. The earlier “pending” amount will either drop off or convert into the final charge.

Cheers,
Afiba

To reiterate - the use of facial recognition technology during the selfie verification process is optional, and drivers can instead choose for their selfie to be verified manually by a member of Bolt’s team. Please let us know if you encounter any difficulties with this process.

We trust that this resolves the matter. If you have any additional questions that have not already been addressed, then please let us know. Otherwise, we will consider this matter to be closed.

Yours sincerely,

Bolt

*Key Findings From Internet Research*
{panel}

* Law No. 124/2024 is supposedly fully aligned with (and effectively incorporates) the GDPR ([link|https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/?t=law]).
* Possible translated version: [+*LINK*+|https://idp.al/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/Law-no.124-2024-DP.pdf] (full Albanian is [here|https://kuvendiwebfiles.blob.core.windows.net/webfiles/202412301451174250ligj%20nr.%20124%2C%20dt.%2019.12.2024.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
* OneTrust - Key Points ([link|https://www.dataguidance.com/notes/albania-privacy-overview])
** GDPR and Law Enforcement Directive fully incorporated. As such, key concepts are the same.
** IDPC is the data protection commissioner ([link|https://idp.al/]). Can launch investigations, suspend unlawful processing and issue fines.
** Requirements for consent and legitimate interest are pretty much identical.
** Minors are anyone under the age of 18. Where under 16, the consent of the parents must be obtained.
** There is no registration or authorisation requirement under the law. However, a {color:#403294}*DPO must be appointed, and details must be notified to the IDPC*{color}. 
*** Also, if controller is not established in Albania, must appoint a {color:#403294}*local representative, and notify the IDPC* {color}of this representative in writing.
** There are no data localisation requirements. EEA states are recognised as ‘adequate’.
** There is no timeframe for notifying data subjects affected by a PDB (although the obligation exists).
** In addition to the usual DSRs, there is a right not to be subject to decisions that result in discrimination based on sensitive data (as part of general ADM rule). Also, {color:#403294}*timeframe for response can be increased from 30 days to 60 days*{color} (not 3 months).
** Data subjects have the right to en effective judicial remedy / compensation. Fines can be up to EUR 20.3m or 4% of global turnover. Criminal liability not explicitly addressed.

price increase reasons. ran in Databricks:


{code:sql}SELECT DISTINCT 
month(x.created) AS MONTH, 
SUM(x.user_price_eur) AS sum_user_price_eur,
COUNT(DISTINCT x.id) AS count_orders,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(x.uncovered_amount/x.eur_currency_rate) AS double),2) AS fp_sum,
ROUND(CAST(SUM(x.initial_failed_payment_amount/x.eur_currency_rate) AS double),2) AS initial_fp_sum
FROM (
WITH order_predictions AS (
SELECT DISTINCT 
order_id,
city_id,
id AS prediction_id,
change_reason,
CASE WHEN type = 'prediction' THEN range_max_price ELSE predicted_price END AS driver_predicted_price,
CASE WHEN type = 'prediction' THEN (CASE WHEN discount_range_max_price IS NOT NULL THEN discount_range_max_price ELSE range_max_price END) ELSE (CASE WHEN discount_price IS NOT NULL THEN discount_price ELSE predicted_price END) END AS rider_predicted_price,
-- "type" = 'prediction' means the price is in a range. for all the other types, it works like upfront. 
-- https://taxify.slack.com/archives/CGLJZE1SA/p1758706871517959?thread_ts=1758698797.701979&cid=CGLJZE1SA
row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id || city_id ORDER BY created DESC) AS ROW_NUMBER_desc,
row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id || city_id ORDER BY created) AS ROW_NUMBER_asc
FROM ng_public_spark.pricing_order_prediction 
WHERE created_date BETWEEN '2025-04-01' AND '2025-06-30'
AND (change_reason IS NULL OR change_reason NOT IN ('driver_cancelled','client_offer_changed'))
),
pricing_recalculation_hint AS (
SELECT DISTINCT 
order_id,
city_id,
hint
FROM immutable_data_live.order_pricing_calculations
WHERE created_date BETWEEN '2025-04-01' AND '2025-06-30'
),
predicted_tolls AS (
SELECT
prediction_id,
SUM(price_component_price) AS predicted_toll_sum
FROM ng_public_spark.etl_pricing_order_price_components 
WHERE created_hour_date BETWEEN '2025-04-01' AND '2025-06-30'
AND price_component_type = 'toll_road'
GROUP BY 1
),
components AS (
SELECT DISTINCT 
final_components.prediction_id,
CASE WHEN (final_components.paid_wait_day_component_final > 0 OR final_components.paid_wait_night_component_final > 0) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS price_increase_has_paid_wait,
(final_components.paid_wait_day_component_final + final_components.paid_wait_night_component_final) * final_components.surge_multiplier AS price_increase_from_wait_time,
CASE WHEN final_components.price_review_component_final > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS price_increase_has_price_review,
final_components.price_review_component_final AS price_increase_from_price_review,
CASE WHEN final_components.toll_road_component_final > COALESCE(ts.predicted_toll_sum,0) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS price_increase_has_additional_toll,
(final_components.toll_road_component_final - COALESCE(ts.predicted_toll_sum,0)) AS price_increase_from_additional_tolls
FROM ng_public_spark.etl_order_price_components final_components
LEFT JOIN predicted_tolls ts ON ts.prediction_id = final_components.prediction_id
WHERE final_components.created_date BETWEEN date '2025-04-01' AND date '2025-06-30'
)
SELECT DISTINCT 
co.uncovered_amount,
co.uncovered_amount/co.eur_currency_rate AS uncovered_eur,
co.initial_failed_payment_amount,
co.initial_failed_payment_amount/co.eur_currency_rate AS initial_failed_payment_amount_eur,
co.user_price_eur,
co.id,
co.eur_currency_rate,
'https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/ride-hailing-order/orders/order/' || co.order_id || '/' || co.city_id AS orderlink,
co.order_id,
co.city_id,
co.country_code,
co.created,
ROUND(co.user_price,2) AS user_price,
p_desc.rider_predicted_price AS last_rider_predicted_price,
p_asc.rider_predicted_price AS first_rider_predicted_price,
ROUND(co.booking_amount_total,2) AS booking_amount_total,
prh.hint AS pricing_recalculation_hint,
CASE WHEN co.user_price > p_asc.rider_predicted_price THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS price_higher_than_first_prediction,
CASE WHEN co.user_price >= p_asc.rider_predicted_price THEN ROUND((co.user_price - p_asc.rider_predicted_price),2) ELSE NULL END AS price_increase_vs_first_prediction,
CASE WHEN co.user_price > co.booking_amount_total THEN ROUND((co.user_price - co.booking_amount_total),2) ELSE NULL END AS price_increase_vs_booked_amount,
CASE WHEN p_desc.rider_predicted_price > p_asc.rider_predicted_price THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS price_increase_has_multiple_predictions,
CASE WHEN p_desc.rider_predicted_price > p_asc.rider_predicted_price THEN (p_desc.rider_predicted_price - p_asc.rider_predicted_price) ELSE NULL END AS price_increase_from_multiple_predictions,
CASE WHEN p_desc.rider_predicted_price > p_asc.rider_predicted_price AND p_desc.change_reason IN ('client_destination_changed','driver_destination_changed','driver_waypoint_changed') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS price_increase_has_dest_change_with_multiple_predictions,
CASE WHEN p_desc.rider_predicted_price > p_asc.rider_predicted_price AND p_desc.change_reason IN ('client_destination_changed','driver_destination_changed','driver_waypoint_changed') THEN (p_desc.rider_predicted_price - p_asc.rider_predicted_price) ELSE NULL END AS price_increase_from_dest_change_with_multiple_predictions,
CASE WHEN p_desc.rider_predicted_price > p_asc.rider_predicted_price AND p_desc.change_reason IN ('custom_pricing_price_confirmation', 'driver_offer_accepted', 'failed_order_price_confirmation') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS price_increase_has_pricing_features_with_multiple_predictions,
CASE WHEN p_desc.rider_predicted_price > p_asc.rider_predicted_price AND p_desc.change_reason IN ('custom_pricing_price_confirmation', 'driver_offer_accepted', 'failed_order_price_confirmation') THEN (p_desc.rider_predicted_price - p_asc.rider_predicted_price) ELSE NULL END AS price_increase_from_pricing_features_with_multiple_predictions,
CASE WHEN COALESCE(co.tips_amount,0) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS price_increase_has_tips,
CASE WHEN COALESCE(co.tips_amount,0) > 0 THEN co.tips_amount ELSE NULL END AS price_increase_from_tips,
c.price_increase_has_paid_wait,
NULLIF(c.price_increase_from_wait_time,0) AS price_increase_from_wait_time,
c.price_increase_has_price_review,
NULLIF(c.price_increase_from_price_review,0) AS price_increase_from_price_review,
c.price_increase_has_additional_toll,
NULLIF(c.price_increase_from_additional_tolls,0) AS price_increase_from_additional_tolls,
CASE WHEN COALESCE(tpr.price,0) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS price_increase_has_driver_manual_correction,
NULLIF(tpr.price,0) AS price_increase_from_driver_manual_correction
FROM ng_public_spark.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders co
JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order_try ot ON co.order_id = ot.order_id AND co.city_id = ot.city_id AND ot.state = 'finished' 
LEFT JOIN order_predictions p_asc ON p_asc.order_id = co.order_id AND p_asc.city_id = co.city_id AND p_asc.ROW_NUMBER_asc = 1
LEFT JOIN order_predictions p_desc ON p_desc.order_id = co.order_id AND p_desc.city_id = co.city_id AND p_desc.ROW_NUMBER_desc = 1
LEFT JOIN pricing_recalculation_hint prh ON prh.order_id = co.order_id AND prh.city_id = co.city_id
LEFT JOIN components c ON c.prediction_id = p_desc.prediction_id
LEFT JOIN ng_public_spark.company_order_try_price_row tpr ON tpr.order_try_id = ot.id AND tpr.city_id = ot.city_id AND tpr.type = 'correction' AND tpr.created_date BETWEEN '2025-04-01' AND '2025-06-30'
WHERE co.created_date BETWEEN '2025-04-01' AND '2025-06-30'
AND ot.created_date BETWEEN '2025-04-01' AND '2025-06-30'
AND co.order_type = 'rides'
AND co.order_state = 'finished'
AND ((co.user_price > co.booking_amount_total) OR (co.user_price > p_asc.rider_predicted_price))
AND COALESCE(co.card_booked_amount,0) > 0
) AS x
--WHERE x.pricing_recalculation_hint IN ('threshold_exceeded','distance_threshold_exceeded')
--WHERE x.price_increase_has_paid_wait = 1
--WHERE x.price_increase_has_dest_change_with_multiple_predictions = 1
--WHERE x.price_increase_has_driver_manual_correction = 1
--WHERE x.price_increase_has_tips = 1
--WHERE x.price_increase_has_additional_toll = 1
--WHERE x.price_increase_has_pricing_features_with_multiple_predictions = 1
--WHERE x.price_increase_has_price_review = 1
GROUP BY 1{code}

*Regarding the data which our users will input into LogicGate:*

For the most part, this is a simple question as most of the information is not personal information and fal

* *Risk management data*: identifiers, descriptions, risk categories, scoring/assessment values, owners, mitigation/control details, supporting evidence or documents.
* *Compliance data*: framework/requirement information, applicability, assessment results, evidence, rationale, ownership, metadata.
* *Policy data*: policy documents and versions, metadata (author, approver, tags), review/approval workflow records, attestations.
* *Audit & issues data*: audit plans, findings, workpapers, evidence, remediation actions, issue logs with owner and status.
* *Integration metadata*: references/IDs for risks, controls, policies or issues when pushing notifications or tickets to Jira, Slack, Gmail, or future connected systems

For personal identifiers in relation to the above, we will be adding owners to risks, requirements, policies, issues and controls. This will include:

* Business contact information (names, titles, emails, departments)
* Workflow metadata relating to employee assignments, approvals, and attestations
* Policy, audit and issue management records containing references to responsible employees and their responsibilities.

In more sensitive cases, should we opt to track incidents within LogicGate in the future, this might include additional data such as nature of injuries sustained, by whom and where.

The more complex part is the fact that users will be uploading evidence of compliance for all our compliance requirements. That evidence can significantly vary from proving that we are compliant by uploading a process or a standard to uploading screenshots of a feature.

I am thinking whether due to the varying nature of evidence that will be uploaded, is it better to assume that sensitive data will be uploaded (let’s suppose driver details for example) and include this or set guidelines for people uploading evidence not to include such information (which does not necessarily prevent them from doing so).

+*Background*+

* Bolt is considering starting an expense management system, and is currently exploring an option for doing so with Yokoy.
** Yokoy = Travleperk company, which specialises in invoice/receipt/transaction management ([link|https://yokoy.io/]). SPand management here is enabled with the use of AI.
** Plan is to implement a short ‘proof of concept’ testing period for their platform and bank cards functionality.
* Request = Review the Order Form and general Service Terms and do a quick red flags check.
** NB. New agreement will be formed after POC period, so this is only temporary.
* Timeline is ASAP. Privacy Team was looped in for the first time on 24 September.

+*Analysis*+

* *General*:
** Risk profile = {color:#ff991f}*Medium*{color} 
*** Limited in scope, and TravelPerk is relatively trustworthy. 
*** However, financially sensitive info, and Bolt is mainly on the hook here.
*** We would ordinarily push for our standard form here. Fine to accept for POC period, but we should push for it later on.
** Data sharing based on legitimate interest. Not a major transparency risk here.
* *Order Form* ([link|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1k-uR91HstysdsM74vf7e7yRday4_Ptkc/edit]) = No comments (/) 
** BoltOps OU is the Bolt party.
** Term is 26 September until 14 January 2026. Separate Service Agreement will follow.
** Incorporates Service Terms and General T&Cs for Debit Card.
* *Service Terms* ([link|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1EF3pyTVjTSrYUHBOJnR-Yav4-nyb-CvC/edit]) = No comments (/) 
** Incorporates Standard Terms, product Specific Terms and Data Processing Addendum.
** Services are generally allowing customers to streamline finance operations through consolidating invoices on a spend management platform.
** Aggregate liability of either party shall not exceed payable by Bolt for the 12 months preceding the incident (7.3).
* *General T&Cs for Debit Card* ([link|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Abaf_nhrEpJdEGNjfI3mJsLbLYI74CJi/edit]) = No comments (/) 
** Governs use of corporate debit card.
** States that personal data must be processed, but does not mention what. Also suggests that data transfers will be taking place to extra-EEA partners (measures not specified) (16).
* *Data Processing Addendum* ([link|https://yokoy.io/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/dpa-250701-en.pdf]) (!) 
** This is a standard document from Yokoy’s website.
** Yokoy is specified as a the *processor* for the purposes of providing the services, and a *controller* for any other purposes set out in Yokoy’s [privacy notice|https://yokoy.io/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/202409_Yokoy-Privacy-Policy-English.pdf]. Bolt is the controller.
*** This raises an overlap risk, as requires clear segregation of purposes and data minimisation.
** Article 28 requirements = Fine.
** T/O measures = Summarised [here|https://trustcenter.travelperk.com/]. Looks reasonably robust, but {color:#ff5630}*would need to be vetted by IS*{color}.
*** NB. Probably not a huge issue, as we already use Travekperk.
** Yokoy must forward DSRRs within 3 days - fine.
** Yokoy must forward authority requests within 3 days - {color:#ff5630}*This is too long*{color}.
** Yokoy will notify PDBs within 24 hours - fine.
** Subprocessers [here|https://trustcenter.travelperk.com/subprocessors] are automatically authorised - Fine, as we already use Travelperk.
*** {color:#ff5630}*Unclear how notices of new sub-processors will be delivered*{color}. Should be in writing/email, and not via website update.
*** NB. Mentions transfers to AWS in USA, although clarifies that datacentre is located in EEA. Seems to also suggest that US data transfers are governed by EU SCCs.
** Bolt has 14-day right to object to new subprocessors - fine.
** Yokoy is required to enter into SCCs where applicable - fine. However, {color:#ff5630}*we have not seen them*{color}.
*** Specified that data is processed in Ireland, Germany, Spain and Switzerland for customers based in EU/EEA, and UK for UK customers.
** Audits can be conducted, but at Bolt’s cost once per year, unless the audit reveals a material breach - fine.
** {color:#ff5630}*Mutual*{color} uncapped indemnity, which is odd - however, core point is that Yokoy will still indemnify for any breach of the DPA or applicable laws.
*** However, {color:#ff5630}*liability is limited in Germany*{color} to “_foreseeable and typical damage according to the type of contract concerned_”. We would ordinarily push for uncapped here.
** Details of processing:
*** Purpose is provision of expense management solutions and providing customer services.
*** {color:#ff5630}*No mention of not using data to train AI models*{color}.
*** Data subjects = Individuals on the platform (i.e., employees).
*** Data = User contact info, content data uploaded by users, “_Google location data… for trip creation_”, invoice information, payment information (including cardholder data, bank account data),and mobile device data.
*** After services terminated, data anonymised within 30 days, except where otherwise required to retain (6 years). Risk here is that, because Yokoy is also a controller, {color:#ff5630}*certain data may be retained beyond our expectations*{color}. We must ensure dataflows are clear, and controller data does not {color:#ff5630}*overlap*{color} with processor data.

+*Key Risks / Mitigations*+

||*Issue*||*Description*||*Mitigation(s)*||*Priority*||
|*Liability*|The indemnity under the DPA is mutual. It is unclear why this is the case, since Bolt is ‘on the hook’ for Yokoy’s non-compliance as a processor.

Hey, [~accountid:5b8d306bfa38ae2c89608b95] ! Sharing here the analysis for OTCs in Romania:

*Executive summary*: the law does not expressly prohibit sale of OTCs online, however, the authorities in Romania want to prevent sale of OTCs via platforms and Bolt’s position is to maintain good relationship with government and authorities hence the blocking of sale of OTC is not opposed.

*Full overview:*

* Law 266/2008 and Order 444/2019 govern online pharmacy operations.
* *Only licensed pharmacies* can sell OTC medicines online, and only with a specific mention in their license. Prescription medicines cannot be sold online.
* Online pharmacies must meet *strict obligations* (license display, full leaflet, link to ANMDM, pharmacist–patient interaction, disclaimers, etc.).
* *Outsourcing is permitted* *only for technical operations*, not for the sale or dispensing of medicines. 
* However, *the transport can be outsourced*, on the basis of contracts with transport companies which can ensure the storage conditions specified by the manufacturer. The beneficiary of the contract must not entrust to any third party any activity which falls under his contract
* If Bolt would be classified as online pharmacy → would require full licensing and compliance (dedicated pharmacist, confidentiality, patient dialogue).
* If Bolt acts as a mere intermediary → must still respect Art. 32(8) Order 444/2019, which prohibits outsourcing of sales/dispensing.
* *The Ministry of Health* has _expressed its view_ in several meetings that online platforms cannot sell OTCs, but this is not expressly prohibited by law,  hence it is considered rather an interpretative guidance rather than a binding rule.
* Key insight from *Glovo’s lawyers*: platforms “operate within a legislative loophole”
* *Licensing compliance risk*: Bolt could be deemed to participate in *unlicensed distribution* of OTC medicine if transactions are interpreted as taking place within its online infrastructure. This may expose the company to fines of up to RON 100,000 (approx. EUR 20,000), or even to criminal liability if such conduct is carried out under conditions that qualify, under criminal law, as criminal offences, e.g., Carrying out a profession or activity without right (Art. 348 of the Criminal Code), sanctioned with up to 1-year imprisonment or fine (legal entities will pay the equivalent fine expressed in daily-fine units for one year of imprisonment). 
** Likewise, *displaying the emblem or trade name of a pharmacy or drugstore by an entity that is not duly authorized under the law* constitutes an administrative offence, punishable by a fine of up to RON 50,000 (approx. EUR 10,000), unless the conduct is so serious as to qualify as a criminal offence under applicable law.
** Note: Administrative fines and criminal sanctions may be imposed cumulatively.
* Delivery compliance risk: The Ministry of Health stated that the “thermal insulation bags” (delivery bags) do not represent vehicles and equipment suitable for the transport of medicines, as required by Art. 40 of Order 444/2019. 
* In March 2025 we had the last update on the topic: the Coalition (which includes the majority of digital platforms in RO) is collaborating with RASCI (Romanian Association of Manufacturers of OTC Medicines, Dietary Supplements and Medical Devices) in order to amend the legislation to allow the delivery of OTCs through digital platforms. RASCI contacted the Ministry of Health and asked to seriously consider changing the law. No updates since then.

As a general comment, although I appreciate that we are only dealing with a POC period here, this is quite a tight timeline for providing full privacy law review, so going forward (particularly if we decide to continue with Yokoy) I would appreciate if I could be added in good time so that I can fully assess and advise on the risks 🙏 

Also, as a general question (?) {color:#4c9aff} {color}{color:#4c9aff}*What is the geographic scope of this arrangement*{color} (i.e., what is the law governing the agreement, where are the parties based, and where are the users based)? In particular, can I assume this agreement is not governed by German law?

----

*Order Form*

* No comments - This does not address privacy law issues (/) 

*Service Terms*

* No comments - This does not address privacy law issues (/) 

*Data Processing* *Addendum* ([+link+|https://yokoy.io/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/dpa-250701-en.pdf])

* These agreements incorporate the DPA, which is Yokoy’s standard agreement available online. This is the main document the privacy team is concerned with.
** I assume that there is limited scope for amending this, but in case there is, then the key issues are below (together with suggested next steps).

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*In short, Column 4 contains recommendations on provisions to include in the current setup (ideally in the DPA). If we cannot include these in the time available, then we can proceed without them for the POC period, provided the business is willing to accept the risks.* (!) 
{panel}

||*Issue*||*Priority*||*Risk*||*Suggested Next Steps* 
*(if we* +*can*+ *amend the DPA before the POC)*||*Suggested Next Steps* 
*(if we* +*cannot*+ *amend the DPA before the POC)*||
|*Indemnity / Liability*
The indemnity for non-compliance under the DPA is mutual / two-way. This is unusual for a controller-processor relationship.
Also, although liability is uncapped, this does not apply where the DPA is governed by German laws.|🔴|For controller-processor relationships, Bolt is primarily the party that is ‘on the hook’ here. As such, such indemnities are typically one-way, rather than mutual - otherwise, Bolt is unnecessarily agreeing to additional liability.
If the scope of the Bolt-Yokoy relationship includes Germany, Yokoy’s liability will be capped to an unreasonably low level. In such circumstances, if Bolt received a fine for Yokoy not complying with privacy laws, Bolt would be extremely limited in the amount it could recover from Yokoy.|Ideally, we would suggest our own Bolt template DPA instead of the Yokoy DPA (although I assume we do not have time to do this).
If we can only recommend amendments to the Yokoy DPA, I would recommend *including our standard controller-processor indemnity clause* - I would be happy to provide this if needed.|Provided that this arrangement is not governed by German law, and given that it is only for a 3-month period, it is *open to the business to accept this risk* and proceed with the DPA as drafted.
If we decide to go ahead with Yokoy after the POC period expires, we should push harder for our standard indemnity provisions.|
|*Retention of data provided by Bolt*
The DPA states that Yokoy can retain personal data after the agreement is terminated for certain purposes, but it does not clearly differentiate _what_ data.|:orange_circle:|There is a risk that Yokoy will continue to use Bolt employee data for its own purposes after the agreement ends - this may result in complaints / questions to us from Bolt employees.|Ideally, we would suggest our own Bolt template DPA instead of the Yokoy DPA (although I assume we do not have time to do this).
If we can only recommend amendments to the Yokoy DPA, I would recommend *including a requirement that any data retained by Yokoy after the agreement terminates must not include personal data originally processed on behalf of Bolt, unless continued retention is required by legal obligation*.|Given that the POC period is only for 3 months, it is *open to the business to accept this risk* and proceed with the DPA as drafted. 
If we decide to go ahead with Yokoy after the POC period expires, we should push harder for including provisions which cover this.|
|*Use of Bolt data for AI training*
Based on a quick skim of Yokoy’s solutions, Yokoy uses AI on its platform. However, the DPA does not contain any provisions saying that Yokoy cannot use data provided by Bolt to train its AI models.|:orange_circle:|If Yokoy uses the data of Bolt employees to train its AI models, Bolt may receive complaints from its employees for not doing enough to keep their personal data safe.|Ideally, we would suggest our own Bolt template DPA instead of the Yokoy DPA (although I assume we do not have time to do this).

If we decide to go ahead with Yokoy after the POC period expires, we should push harder for including provisions which cover this.|
|*Lack of vetting of Yokoy measures*
I assume that InfoSec has not reviewed the security measures implemented by Yokoy? In any cases, we (the Privacy Team) have no visibility of the data transfer mechanisms that Yokoy has entered into with its sub-processors.|:green:|As the controller here, Bolt is required to conduct adequate diligence on its processors. It may be difficult to argue this given that these review steps have not yet been followed.
The main risk here is that if we are sending Yokoy data and it turns out Yokoy’s security measures are not up to scratch (which we have not checked), the data may be leaked as a result of a data breach on Yokoy’s side. Affected individuals would be more likely to go after Bolt in such circumstances.|If there is time, it would be *preferable for InfoSec to be looped* in to review Yokoy’s security measures, and for us to ask Yokoy to provide a sample of its agreements with its sub-processors. 
However, I assume this is not feasible in the time available, so it is more of an FYI for now.|Given that the POC period is only for 3 months, it is *open to the business to accept this risk* and proceed with the DPA as drafted. This is ultimately low risk, and so is not a blocker.

h2. *Clarification*

*Context:*

There are 3 ways in which a service can get its role:
- if one is defined in the config
- the Builder-generated role (each service receives a different role from Builder)
- a default role, common for all the services.
When reading dynamic-config values:
- All the services use the default role
- The default role also has write permissions

*Problem*: All services could write dynamic-config values.

*Solution*: Remove the write permission from the default role and grant write permission to the Builder-generated role of the Dynamic-Config Service.

*Steps:*

# Talk to SRE to assign write permission for the dynamic-config S3 bucket for the Builder-generated role of the dynamic-config service. They can use the files in s3-confligless to identify the Builder-generated role for the Dynamic-Config Service [prelive|https://github.com/bolteu/s3-configless/blob/main/PRELIVE/configless-roles-prelive0/eu-central-1/dynamicconfig/terragrunt.hcl.json] and [live|https://github.com/bolteu/s3-configless/blob/main/LIVE/configless-roles-live0/eu-central-1/dynamicconfig/terragrunt.hcl.json])
# Wait.
# Add {{skipDefaultRole: true}} in the Dynamic-Config service's [config|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/develop/src/foundation/backend/dynamic_config/main/config/config.defaults.production.ts#L8]. This will make it assume the Builder-assigned role instead.
# Test that the Dynamic-Config Service is able to write configs.
# Talk to SRE to remove the write permission from the default role (default role ARN [prelive|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-nodejs-common/blob/b102c1c4e97a4870b4991f1a518a4d85a93b0dbe/src/async/aws/AwsUtils.ts#L20] and [live|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-nodejs-common/blob/b102c1c4e97a4870b4991f1a518a4d85a93b0dbe/src/async/aws/AwsUtils.ts#L18])

Do those steps first for PRELIVE, then for LIVE.

h2. Scores

Time Criticality: 5 (in one Q)
Risk Reduction: 8 (improves security in more components - all users of dynamic config)
Business Value: 1 (it’s not a user/dev journey, it automates nothing)
Job size: 3 (up to 1 week, could be less but there are some async steps so 1 week is safer estimation)
Opportunity: 8 (dynamic-config is tier 2)
